scope: Owning-guest-thread posted messages and coalesced USER timers, with real monotonic deadlines and finite native AOT callback dispatch.
timers: Period clamped to 10..2147483647 milliseconds. HWND0 timers receive process-unique nonzero IDs. Existing owner/window/ID resets deadline and callback. Retrieval generates WM_TIMER only after matching posted messages; overdue periods coalesce. KillTimer and window destruction remove future timers, preserving messages already queued.
delivery: DispatchMessageA calls the finite original TIMERPROC with HWND, WM_TIMER, ID and current GetTickCount on the calling guest thread using tribes_call_guest. No guest callback runs on the native audio thread. Hidden window messages call their retained original WNDPROC.
queues: Created lazily per configured TEB thread or on catalog window creation. Registry/queue synchronization uses pthread mutex and conditions. GetMessage waits on actual posts or matching timer deadlines; WM_QUIT bypasses filters and returns zero. Guest thread finalization removes queue and timers.
memory: Legacy x86 28-byte MSG prefix; checked guest reads/writes and CPU-aware stdcall callbacks use existing instrumentation. Host queue nodes are never exposed as guest pointers.
limits: Native SDL input conversion and native SDL window WNDPROC dispatch remain explicit integration boundaries.
Keyboard TranslateMessage, broadcast posting and PeekMessage queue-category flags remain explicit stops.
Catalog supports current top-level windows, not child-window descendant filtering.
Message cursor coordinates are zero until native input integration; no mouse-input acceptance is claimed.
No general sent-message API or nested GUI modal-loop implementation.
validation: Normal, checked-memory and thread-sanitizer component tests exercise deadlines, reset/cancel/coalescing, queue priority, blocking wakeups, owning-thread callback ABI and thread cleanup. Original-engine registration and callback execution require separate full-app evidence.
